description:
Repro (0a1d44728): dbg(Kernel.apply(Kernel, :abs, [-2])) -> error[macro/not-required]: remote macro Kernel.apply/3 requires require Kernel (or resolve/unknown-import 'module Kernel does not export apply/3', depending on whether Kernel's definition is published when the call expands). Elixir prints 2. Unqualified apply(Kernel, :abs, [-2]) prints 2. With 'require Kernel' at the top of the user file the qualified call prints 2.

It is not about apply. apply/3 is a defmacro (lib/kernel.fz:238, :242) and every qualified call to a Kernel macro fails the same way: Kernel.&&(true, 3), Kernel.if(true, do: 1, else: 2). Kernel.abs(-2) works because abs is a function.

Cause: Elixir says importing a module requires it, and Kernel is imported everywhere. fz keeps a separate per-source set of required modules:
- required_remote_macros is created empty per source session (src/compiler2/source_publish.rs:593), filled only by apply_require (:1474-1509, record_required_remote_macros :1752), and copied into the expander (jobs/source.rs:539, world.rs:3720).
- apply_import (source_publish.rs:1616-1654) records nothing there.
- The expander refuses a remote macro whose module is not in that set (quoted_expander.rs:461, :488, :1289); when the module's definition is not yet published and it is a runtime module it returns Ok(None) (:422-424) and the call falls to function resolution, which reports unknown-import.
- The prelude's 'import Kernel, only: [...]' (lib/runtime.fz:30-49) reaches user files for unqualified names but the required set does not. Probes: 'require Kernel' in the prelude fails (Kernel not defined yet); 'require Kernel, only: [...]' in the prelude compiles but user files still fail.

Direction to spike before any page: one rule, as in Elixir: a module in scope by import is required. Ask the scope the question the import already answers, so the prelude's import of Kernel covers every source, and see whether the separate required set can then hold only what 'require' alone adds, or disappear.

Done when: an oracle fixture calls Kernel macros by qualified name (apply/3 with a named function and with :+, &&, if) without writing require, and a user module's macro is callable qualified after 'import M' alone, matching Elixir on interp, run and build; a remote macro of a module that is neither imported nor required is still refused.
title: A module that is imported is also required, so Kernel's macros are callable by their qualified name
